correctness.rationale: The coefficient of each vertex in part i of a square is S-Q_i. Hence all Q_i=S and (r-1)S=0, giving exactly the two cases. The explicit quadratic Gauss-sum fiber formulas count all rational points, including singleton parts and nonzero shared values at characteristic resonance. Over an algebraic closure, binary cones split into two lines and higher rank quadratic cones are irreducible; Galois acts by a simultaneous sign swap. Hyperbolic-plane arguments and a sign-difference construction prove both span formulas. The resonant fiber-product ring is flat over its shared-value line; its r-1 equations form a generically smooth complete intersection with no vertical components, so it is geometrically reduced and equidimensional. The standalone checker exhaustively verified counts and spans in twenty-one independent finite-field configurations including F9. Limits: exhaustive finite experiments do not certify untested infinite cases or algebraic geometry without the proof.

value.rationale: The square-zero points are fixed-zero states of a natural quadratic evolution operator. For every complete multipartite graph over every odd finite field, one theorem simultaneously determines rational points, the exact resonance jump in geometric dimension, geometric and rational component counts away from resonance, and the linear span generated by zero states. Sharp contrasting examples include K_(2,2) with 1 point over F3 and 81 over F5, and K_(p+1) with 2^p rational lines spanning the entire algebra exactly at characteristic p. These are structural arithmetic and geometric invariants across an unbounded family, not a parameter-renaming or a small isolated computation. The use of standard finite-field quadratic-count lemmas is acknowledged.
